candidates.title: The Olympia & Sand Creek Ry.
candidates.excerpt: A time for a change So, you want to build a railroad, but perhaps you’re having a hard time finding a dedicated space for a layout. Or maybe you have the space, but you lack the ability to work well with small details, such as those found on N and HO scale models. And perhaps you’d like a large railroad, but you’re just overwhelmed by the cost in time and resources to build one. If any or all of those concerns fit your situation, then consider building a narrow gauge O scale sectional layout, such as my Olympia & Sand Creek Ry. The layout, also known as just “Olympia,” was constructed in three distinct sections over a 12-year period. Each section contained its own set of approachable projects, spreading the cost and modeling work over time. The railroad is built into furniture-like shadowboxes, giving the layout a museum-quality finish, which allows it to comfortably blend into the living spaces that also need to be used by others. candidates.title: Arken Intermodal Terminal achieves near-doubled yard capacity
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Gothenburg has significantly increased yard capacity at Arken Intermodal Terminal through a reconfiguration of the railway track layout, freeing up approximately 4,000 square metres of additional yard space for trailers and other units. The result is an increase of almost double the previous yard capacity from a five percent expansion in available space. Arken Intermodal Terminal is one of Sweden’s largest intermodal terminals and a key hub for transfers between rail, road and sea. Growing cargo volumes over time had pushed capacity in certain flows close to its limit, with yard space identified as the primary constraint. The capacity improvement was achieved by rebuilding one of the through tracks at the terminal to release the additional yard area, demonstrating that smarter use of existing infrastructure can deliver substantial gains without the need for large-scale construction. candidates.title: Can carriers avoid overcapacity in 2027?
candidates.excerpt: Can carriers avoid overcapacity in 2027? The backdrop is difficult to ignore. Around 5 mteu of new capacity has been ordered in each of the past three years, pushing the orderbook-to-fleet ratio to approximately 45%, its highest level since 2009. The orderbook is fast approaching 16 mteu, with September the second-busiest contracting month on record at 1.1 mteu, following major orders from the world’s two largest carriers: MSC (20 × 24,000 teu) and Maersk (20 × 18,600 teu). The counterargument is that traditional supply-demand fundamentals no longer tell the whole story. Geopolitical disruption, port congestion and longer sailing distances have become increasingly influential, absorbing capacity and limiting the amount of nominal fleet capacity available to carry cargo. Ultimately, the 2027 outcome will depend on whether demand growth, slow steaming and congestion can absorb capacity faster than new ships enter service. Our view? They won’t. candidates.excerpt: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators Kroll and StepStone Group have launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators to provide greater transparency into the use of non-cash interest in private credit markets. The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012. They measure PIK as a proportion of interest income, the percentage of loans with an active PIK component by deal count, and their share of outstanding principal. The indicators will also allow investors to compare PIK usage across geographies, sectors and borrower sizes. The launch comes as the firms’ data suggests PIK usage is moderating, with non-cash interest accounting for 2.86 per cent of interest income on loans originated globally over the previous 12 months, as of 10 October 2026. The new container vessel portfolio comprises three primary variants: twenty 19,000 teu ships, twelve units of 22,000 teu ships and twenty 24,000 teu ships. Last week MSC contracted twenty 24,000 teu vessels with the Chinese shipbuilder. “Hengli Heavy Industry continues to deepen cooperation with major global liner and shipping groups, contributing to the green upgrading of global shipping across container, oil, dry bulk and emerging ammonia trades,” stated the shipyard. candidates.excerpt: CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering expects profit surge Container ship newbuild deals drive the company’s hitting 217% of its annual order target in nine months CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering has forecast a notable jump in profits for the first nine months of 2026. The company projects its net profit attributable to owners of the parent for the January–September period to be between RMB1.10 billion and RMB 1.25 billion, a year-on-year increase of RMB 444.88 million to RMB 594.88 million, or a growth rate ranging from 67.91% to 90.80%. Its net profit attributable to parent owners is expected to hit RMB1 billion to RMB1.15 billion over the same timeframe, rising RMB 394.89 million to RMB 544.89 million from the 2025 comparable period, up 65.26% to 90.05% year on year. The strong expected performance stems from buoyant market conditions across the shipbuilding sector and solid operational execution by the firm.
